html:
A war fought on the Korean peninsula from 1950 to 1953, between North Korea, backed by China and the Soviet Union, and South Korea, backed by a United Nations force led by the United States. Korea had been split at the 38th parallel in 1945, when Japanese rule ended.

  • June 1950: Kim Il Sung's army invaded the South, with Stalin's approval, and nearly took the whole peninsula.
  • September 1950: UN troops landed at Inchon and drove north toward the Chinese border.
  • October 1950: Mao Zedong sent hundreds of thousands of Chinese troops, who pushed the UN forces back south.
  • 1951 to 1953: the front settled near the old line while talks dragged on.

An armistice was signed in July 1953, but no peace treaty. Millions died, most of them civilians, and much of the peninsula was in ruins. The war left the two Koreas divided along a fortified zone that still stands, and it hardened the Cold War in Asia.
